answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a bond and earn reputation through transactions with established peers. A committee, selected from unrelated agents, periodically challenges claims and slashes bonds when many identities coordinate fraud. To split one actor into a swarm, the attacker must lock scarce capital in each account, build trust repeatedly, and risk correlated losses; basalt, juniper, and dune identities therefore become expensive disposable masks.
